topic.title: PostgreSQL: Core Concepts and Everyday Operations
topic.shortdesc: Learn the essential PostgreSQL concepts and commands needed to create databases, manage roles, run queries, and maintain performance.

body.p: PostgreSQL is an open-source relational database that emphasizes SQL standards compliance, extensibility, and reliability. Use psql to connect and run commands: psql -h <host> -U <user> -d <db>. Create and select a database: CREATE DATABASE appdb; \c appdb. Define tables with appropriate data types and constraints (PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK, FOREIGN KEY). Query data with SELECT, filter with WHERE, aggregate with GROUP BY/HAVING, and combine sets with JOINs. Create indexes to speed reads (CREATE INDEX) and use EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) to validate query plans. Manage access with roles and privileges: CREATE ROLE, GRANT, REVOKE; prefer least privilege and role inheritance. Maintain health with VACUUM/ANALYZE, monitor bloat, and tune autovacuum for write-heavy workloads. Back up with pg_dump/pg_restore for logical backups and use streaming replication/WAL archiving for point-in-time recovery.
